data.narrative:
Aigen is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Kenny Lee (ex-Weblife.io) and Rich Wurden (ex-Tesla). The target has raised approximately $23.7M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises one public comparable and eight private companies in the robotics and manufacturing sector at similar stages, including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Divergent, and Exotec.

Two valuation methods triangulate Aigen's value. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement to the $24M total raised proxy, implying $45M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—yields a median valuation of $1.8B, with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide implied range: $38M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $898M. This substantial spread reflects the tension between raised-capital-based floor methods and peer-comparable ceiling methods in an early-stage, capital-intensive sector. The stage-progression method supports a materially lower valuation; peer comps suggest substantially higher value. Key uncertainties include the relative maturity and revenue traction of peer companies versus Aigen, and whether public market comparables more accurately reflect current private market pricing in this sector.
